description: The bar chart illustrates the accuracy of various model variants in a morphosyntactic probing task, comparing the performance of randomly initialized models under different perturbation conditions against the unperturbed trained model. The horizontal axis displays different model configurations, categorized into three groups: embedding and first layer probes (blue bars), random models with pre-trained embedding layers (green bars), and random models with random embedding layers (red bars), culminating in the unperturbed trained model (orange bars). The vertical axis represents accuracy, ranging from 70 to 95. The blue bars, representing the embedding and first layer probes, show accuracies around 81 and 83, respectively. The green bars, corresponding to random models with pre-trained embeddings, exhibit accuracies between 80 and 83, with slight variations across different perturbation types (e.g., +B2, +L2, +R2, +permute). The red bars, indicating random models with random embeddings, show lower accuracies, generally around 73 to 75, with some variation depending on the perturbation. The orange bars, representing the unperturbed trained models, show the highest accuracy, with values around 91 and 92, indicating that the fully trained models outperform all random variants. The chart highlights that the accuracy decreases significantly when both the embedding and subsequent layers are randomly initialized, and that the perturbation type has a minor impact on performance within each category.
